title: Tajik Cyrillic
done when: You can read any Tajik word aloud from Cyrillic, including ғ, ӣ, қ, ӯ, ҳ and ҷ, and write a sentence you hear in Cyrillic with the right spelling of the izofat and of -ро. This stage is Part A of the chapter.

title: Core phrases in Cyrillic
done when: You can read the Tajik column of the chapter aloud at speaking speed without the transliteration, and write ten of its phrases in Cyrillic from memory.

title: Persian script
done when: You can name all 32 letters in each of their shapes, say which letters do not join, and read a short unvowelled word by supplying its vowels. This stage is Part B of the chapter.

title: Moving between the scripts
done when: You can rewrite ten core phrases from Cyrillic into Persian script and back, and explain each spelling that the sound alone does not give you. This stage is Part C of the chapter.

title: Sounds and spelling
done when: You can say how each Tajik vowel is written in both scripts and how an Iranian speaker pronounces the same word.

title: Language foundations
done when: You can name the izofat, the object marker and the two verb stems in a sentence, and turn five spoken Tajik sentences into written Tajik.

title: Directions and navigation
done when: You can read the chapter's phrases aloud from the Persian-script column alone, and ask for and confirm directions in writing in either script.

title: Transportation
done when: You can read a ticket or a timetable word in either script, and say which transport words change in Iran.

title: Restaurants
done when: You can read a menu line in either script and order, with a substitution, in writing.

title: Shopping
done when: You can read prices and sizes in Persian digits and ask the price and decline politely in writing.

title: Hotels
done when: You can fill in a check-in form in Cyrillic and report a problem with the room in writing.

title: Tajik, Iranian Persian and Dari
done when: For twenty everyday words you can give the Tajik and the Iranian form, and you can restate a Tajik sentence so that an Iranian speaker follows it.

title: Work and business
done when: You can introduce yourself and your role in the formal register, and write a three-line email in Cyrillic and in Persian script with the correct opening and closing.
